title: Hello World
summary: A client talks to a single server.

lesson.problem: A user wants to reach your application. Where does the request go?
why: Every system starts here: one client sends a request, one server handles it and sends back a response. The server runs the code, keeps the data, and does everything else.
This is the right design for a prototype, an internal tool or anything with a handful of users. It is cheap, easy to deploy and easy to reason about.
takeaways: The server is a single point of failure: if it goes down, everything goes down.
It can only grow vertically (a bigger machine), and that has a ceiling.
Start simple. Add components only when a real problem asks for them.
